rules: N active electrons in M active orbitals, exactly two integers; a third element is an input error. Only installed catalogs run (§catalog).

Molecule multiplicity: 1 for even N, 2 for odd N (no installed catalog has odd N); any other value is the error above. The spin manifolds are chosen by §sa_reks_2spin / §si_reks_2spin or the ladder (§spin-manifolds).
REKS.brief: Active space `[N, M]`: N active electrons in M active orbitals; selects the catalog.

rules: Flat list = one block on one spin manifold, e.g. `["PPS1", "OSS1", "OSS2"]` or by local index `[0, 1, 2]`. Elements: configuration names, local integer indices, or bulk tokens (§bulk-tokens).
A configuration may not repeat within a block: an SA block is a weighted list (§bulk-tokens).
Nested list = one block per spin manifold, e.g. `[["PPS1", "OSS1"], ["T_PPS1"]]`, mapped to manifolds by ladder position or by `SA_REKS_2SPIN` (§spin-manifolds).
Absent: the catalog's `sa_default` pool on 2S = 0. Defaults: `REKS(2,2)` `[PPS1, OSS1]`, `REKS(4,4)` `[PPS1, OSS1, OSS2]`, `REKS(6,6)` `[PPS1, OSS1, OSS2, OSS3]`.
Check `sum = 1.000000` and that every `SA_REKS_EXTRA` determinant of the input is listed (`Extra1`, …).
SA_REKS_CONFIGS.brief: SA-REKS configuration pool: one block (flat list) or one block per spin manifold (nested list) of names, indices or bulk tokens.

rules: One integer 2S per SA block (explicit mode, §spin-manifolds). Entries are pairwise distinct, in any order (re-sorted ascending).
Without `SA_REKS_CONFIGS` only `[0]` is accepted; any other value is an input error. States of 2S > 0 on the default ensemble: §si_reks_2spin.
SA_REKS_2SPIN.brief: Spin manifold 2S of each SA block, one integer per block.

rules: One non-negative weight per SA pool entry, in the order typed (concatenated block order, then the `SA_REKS_EXTRA` determinants), summing to 1.0 (tolerance 10^{-8}). Omitted: uniform 1/n.
A configuration or extra determinant with weight 0 leaves the SA ensemble; a zero-weight configuration that is also an SI member has its SI-only geminals' FONs optimized after the SCF.
If `SA_REKS_2SPIN` lists manifolds out of ascending-2S order, configurations and weights are re-sorted jointly into ascending 2S; a weight still matches the configuration in the order typed.
SA_REKS_WEIGHTS.brief: Weights of the SA pool entries, configurations first, then the `sa_reks_extra` determinants; non-negative, summing to 1.

rules: Each element is a Slater determinant given as an occupation vector `[alpha(M) | beta(M)]` of length 2M, 0/1 entries summing to N; the call above is the all-α determinant of REKS(4,4).

Each determinant joins the SA ensemble with a fixed weight from the tail of `SA_REKS_WEIGHTS`, adds its Kohn–Sham energy to E_{SA}, carries no FON, and changes the SA orbitals and with them every SI state. It never enters an SI cassette.
Recommended: the all-α determinant in every SA-REKS ensemble, for SCF stability and the shape of the orbitals. The code does not add it by default.
SA_REKS_EXTRA.brief: Extra Slater determinants of the SA ensemble, as occupation vectors; each has its own weight, carries no FON and enters no SI cassette.

rules: 3-level `[[[...], ...], [[...], ...], ...]`: one group of cassettes per outer entry, each group mapped to a spin manifold like the SA blocks (ladder position or `SI_REKS_2SPIN`). The call above is one group of four cassettes, each with its own states (third fragment; energies: §explicit-input). A cassette is a set of names, indices or bulk tokens (§bulk-tokens); a repeated selection is kept at its first position. First two fragments: `[[["full"]], [["full"]]]` with `SI_REKS_2SPIN` `[0, 2]`.

2-level `[[...], [...], ...]`: the cassettes of a single group on the run's lowest manifold (or the one `SI_REKS_2SPIN` names); legal only when `SI_REKS_2SPIN` is absent or has length 1. The 3-level form without `SI_REKS_2SPIN` maps group 0 to ladder position 0, the catalog's first spin sector; the two forms coincide when that is the run's lowest manifold, as in the call above.
Absent: one cassette spanning the whole configuration block of the run's lowest (or `SI_REKS_2SPIN`-chosen) manifold. `[[]]` runs no SI step and sets no `SSR` arrays.

A flat list of names (`["PPS1", "OSS1"]`) is an input error: `SI_REKS_CONFIGS: scalar elements are not a cassette form; use a list of cassettes [[...], ...] (2-level) or cassette groups [[[...]], ...] (3-level).`
`Wfn storage` `none` in `SI pools` means no per-state `SSR … K=e` analysis arrays and no natural-orbital, NTO or NDO Molden files for that cassette (§si_reks_store_states).
Each cassette opens with a `State interaction: cassette e` header; its 2S tag appears when the run has more than one spin manifold.

Two or more cassettes of one 2S add `Alternative configuration lists` after `State summary` (third fragment): the states of the later cassettes with energies relative to S0 and to their own lowest state, the closest state of the first list by weight overlap, and the main configurations.
SI_REKS_CONFIGS.brief: SI-SA-REKS cassettes: the configuration sets whose secular equations give the states, in groups per spin manifold.

rules: One integer 2S per SI group (explicit mode, §spin-manifolds), pairwise distinct, in any order; more than one entry requires the 3-level `si_reks_configs` form. The 2-level form is one group of cassettes on one manifold. Two entries with a 2-level `si_reks_configs` stop the run: `REKS input error: SI_REKS_2SPIN has 2 labels (one per SI group), which requires the 3-level SI_REKS_CONFIGS form [[[...]], ...] (one group of cassettes per label); got a 2-level list of cassettes.`
`[x]` alone: the default SA ensemble on 2S = 0 and the default SI cassette on 2S = x (§input-patterns).

Sets the order of the SI cassettes: the spin groups follow this list, the cassettes of a group the order of its `SI_REKS_CONFIGS` block. The per-cassette lists §si_reks_grad, §si_reks_nac, §si_reks_property_for and §si_reks_store_states take their entries in this order: with `[2, 0]` entry 0 is the triplet cassette. The printed index K and the `K=e`, `CASSETTE e` names run in ascending 2S (the triplet is K = 1). Without the option (ladder) both orders are ascending 2S (§cassette-order).
SI_REKS_2SPIN.brief: 2S of each SI group; more than one entry requires the 3-level `si_reks_configs` form.

rules: States per cassette listed in the per-state and pair tables; `0` = none, `-1` = all, on a Davidson cassette the 50 lowest (§si-solver).
Properties are computed for max(print, store) states (§si_reks_store_states). Counts are clamped to the number of physical states.
SI_REKS_PRINT_STATES.brief: States per cassette whose per-state and pair tables are printed; 0 = none, -1 = all.

SI_REKS_STORE_STATES.default: all; the first 10 if `M ≥ 6` and > 10 configurations
rules: One integer per cassette, entry t = the t-th cassette in the spin order of §si_reks_2spin (§cassette-order): states whose properties are stored on the wavefunction (array variables, Molden and cube files); `0` = none, `-1` = all, on a Davidson cassette the 50 lowest (§si-solver).
Roots requested in `SI_REKS_GRAD`, `SI_REKS_NAC`, `SI_REKS_PROPERTY_FOR` keep their eigenvectors regardless.
SI_REKS_STORE_STATES.brief: States per cassette whose properties are stored on the wavefunction (arrays, Molden and cube files); 0 = none, -1 = all.

rules: Property blocks to compute, print and store. Unset: every block except multipoles above order 2. `[]`: `TRANSITION_DIPOLE` and `NO_OCCUPATIONS`. A list: these two plus the listed names.

Names: `DIPOLE`, `QUADRUPOLE`, `MULTIPOLE(n)`, `TRANSITION_DIPOLE`, `TRANSITION_QUADRUPOLE`, `E_TDM_VEL`, `M_TDM`, `MULLIKEN_CHARGES`, `LOWDIN_CHARGES`, `MULLIKEN_SPINS`, `LOWDIN_SPINS`, `TRANSITION_CHARGES`, `MAYER_INDICES`, `WIBERG_LOWDIN_INDICES`, `NO_OCCUPATIONS`, `DENSITIES`, `RADICAL`, `NTO`, `EXCITON`, `FRAGMENT_COUPLINGS`, `ALL`, case-insensitive; each property entry names its switch (§properties). `MULLIKEN_SPINS`, `LOWDIN_SPINS` act on 2S > 0 cassettes (§atomic-spins).

A block another listed block needs is computed without being printed or stored: `RADICAL` needs `NO_OCCUPATIONS`, `FRAGMENT_COUPLINGS` the state and transition charges and, in a 2S > 0 cassette, the Löwdin spins.

`MULTIPOLE(n)` adds `DIPOLE` and `TRANSITION_DIPOLE`, for n ≥ 2 `QUADRUPOLE` and `TRANSITION_QUADRUPOLE`, for n ≥ 3 the multipoles of order 3..n. `ALL` switches on every name except `MULTIPOLE(n)`: `["ALL", "MULTIPOLE(4)"]` adds both.

`State analysis` lists every name with a description, names not run struck through; with `SI_REKS_PROPERTY_FOR` it adds the states of each cassette that receive relaxed properties (and EKT when `REKS_EKT` is true).
SI_REKS_ANALYSIS.brief: State-property blocks of the SI states to compute, print and store (moments, charges, bond indices, NTO, exciton, …).

rules: Smallest state-to-state change of a charge, spin population or bond index that is printed (§atomic-charges, §atomic-spins).
SI_REKS_ANALYSIS_CHANGE_MIN.brief: Smallest state-to-state change of a charge or bond index that is printed.

rules: Eigenvectors of the SI overlap with s ≤ cutoff · s_{max} form the null space and are removed before diagonalization (§si-matrices).
Ghost roots (configurations with s just above the cutoff): §ssr-states.

The printed σ = cutoff · s_{max}: `Regularization … sigma = σ: the N configurations span r dimensions (K overlap null modes removed)`. A larger cutoff removes more modes; the number of roots is capped by r.
Large active spaces, spurious lowest root: signs and the value 1e-4 in §diag-ghost-states.
SI_REKS_OVERLAP_CUTOFF.brief: Overlap eigenvalues `s ≤ cutoff · s_{max}` of the SI basis are treated as null space and dropped.

rules: `DIRECT`: every root, LAPACK on the dense Hamiltonian of the cassette. `DAVIDSON`: the lowest roots, block Davidson on the sparse Hamiltonian; how many: §si-solver. `AUTO`: per cassette, `DIRECT` up to 4000 configurations, `DAVIDSON` above; the catalogs shipped with Psi4 stay below.

On a Davidson cassette `SSR ENERGIES K=e` holds the computed roots, and a count `-1` in `SI_REKS_PRINT_STATES`, `SI_REKS_STORE_STATES`, `SI_REKS_GRAD` or `SI_REKS_PROPERTY_FOR` stands for the 50 lowest roots.
SI_REKS_SOLVER.brief: Eigensolver of each SI cassette: LAPACK on every root, or Davidson on the lowest roots.

rules: Residual norm ‖(A − θ) x‖_{2} (E_{h}) every Davidson root converges to, A the SI Hamiltonian in the orthonormalized configuration basis (§si-solver). A root whose residual stalls at the rounding level of its product is accepted there, and that level is printed.
A value ≤ 0 stops the run: `SI_REKS_DAVIDSON_R_CONVERGENCE is …; it must be positive (residual norm in Eh, default 1e-12).`
SI_REKS_DAVIDSON_R_CONVERGENCE.brief: Residual norm in E_h each Davidson root of the SI problem converges to.

rules: Orbital count of each two-electron geminal: N/2 integers, each in [2, 8], summing to M. Empty (default): every geminal spans 2 orbitals.
A width-w geminal holds 2 electrons in w orbitals; its configurations carry orbital-letter suffixes (`OSSa1`, `DESb1`).
Selects the catalog `reks{N}{M}_u{w0}{w1}…`; the installed ones are listed above.
REKS_GEMINAL_WIDTHS.brief: Width (orbital count) of each geminal, N/2 integers summing to M; selects the catalog `reks{N}{M}_u{w0}{w1}…`.

rules: Roots whose gradients are computed, one inner list per cassette; inner list t = the t-th cassette in the spin order of §si_reks_2spin (§cassette-order; with `si_reks_2spin` `[2, 0]` list 0 is the triplet cassette); roots as in §ssr-states. Inner list `[-1]` = all roots of that cassette (`[[-1]]`), on a Davidson cassette the 50 lowest; a flat `[-1]` is an input error. More inner lists than SI cassettes stop the run before the SCF: `REKS input error: SI_REKS_GRAD: 2 order list(s) for 1 SI cassette(s).`

The followed root, marked `*` in `Gradient request`, is the first entry of the first non-empty inner list (`-1` → root 0). Without `SI_REKS_GRAD` it is the lowest root index in the pairs of the first non-empty `SI_REKS_NAC` list.

With a followed root, `CURRENT ENERGY` is its energy, also stored as `REKS TARGET STATE ENERGY`, in `energy()` and `gradient()`; `gradient()` returns its gradient (§state-gradient). Without a followed root: §explicit-input.
`CURRENT DIPOLE` is the relaxed dipole of the followed root when `SI_REKS_PROPERTY_FOR` lists that root, and is unset otherwise.
Triplet gradient of `reks [2, 2]`: the triplet-gradient worked input (§worked-inputs), with `si_reks_grad` `[[], [0]]` following T1 of cassette 1.
SI_REKS_GRAD.brief: Roots whose analytic gradients are computed, per cassette; the first listed root is followed (`CURRENT ENERGY`, returned gradient).

rules: Pairs `[I, J]` per SI cassette, in the spin order of §si_reks_2spin (§cassette-order), `[[[I, J], ...], ...]`, or `ALL`; the call above couples S1 and S2 of cassette 0. Computed in `gradient()`; the roots of each pair join the gradient targets.
Publishes `SSR NAC I J CASSETTE e` (1/bohr, §nac) and the conical-intersection topography `SSR CI TOPOGRAPHY I J CASSETTE e` (§ci-topography); e is the printed cassette index K (ascending 2S).
Without `SI_REKS_GRAD` the followed root: §si_reks_grad.
SI_REKS_NAC.brief: Root pairs `[I, J]` per cassette whose nonadiabatic couplings and conical-intersection topography are computed.

rules: States evaluated with the relaxed density: dipole, quadrupole, Mulliken/Löwdin charges, Mayer/Wiberg indices (§relaxed-properties, §relaxed-bond-indices).
Entries: indices or labels, ranges, lists (`"S0..5"`, `"T1"`), inside the per-cassette inner lists (`[["S0..1"]]`), in the spin order of §si_reks_2spin (§cassette-order); a flat list is rejected.
SI_REKS_PROPERTY_FOR.brief: States, per cassette, whose dipole, quadrupole, charges and bond indices are evaluated with the relaxed (CP-REKS) density.

rules: Extended Koopmans ionization energies, pole strengths and Dyson orbitals for the `SI_REKS_PROPERTY_FOR` states (§ekt-states), otherwise for the SA ensemble (§ekt-ensemble).
REKS_EKT.brief: Enables EKT: ionization energies, pole strengths and Dyson orbitals of the `si_reks_property_for` states or of the SA ensemble.

REKS_EKT_OCC_TOL.brief: Cutoff on the density eigenvalues: those at or below it are dropped from the EKT metric.
rules: Density eigenvalues at or below this are dropped from the EKT metric.
CP-REKS (Z-vector) residual threshold, relative to max(1, ‖b‖). One solve serves the relaxed properties, gradients and NACs of the run.
The solver block is printed when `SI_REKS_PROPERTY_FOR` names states, or in `gradient()` with `SI_REKS_GRAD` or `SI_REKS_NAC`, at `REKS_REPORT_LEVEL` ≥ 2 and Psi4 `PRINT` ≥ 1 (defaults).
Converged: `Remain` reaches 0 and the block ends with `Z-vectors converged in N iterations.`. Non-convergence ends the run with `no convergence in N rounds`.

A target t closes at max(threshold, 10 ε ‖A‖ ‖Z_{t}‖), ε the machine epsilon, ‖A‖ = max(max_{i} |A_{ii}|, max ‖A d‖ over the unit search directions d): below that the residual is roundoff of the operator. Targets closed at this floor are counted after the converged line (`N target(s) closed at the roundoff floor 10 eps |A| |Z|`). When the explicit residual of a target exceeds this bound, every open target continues from its explicit residual in a new search space.
REKS_CPREKS_CONV.brief: Residual threshold of the CP-REKS (Z-vector) solver. `reks_cpreks_maxiter` (200) bounds its rounds.

REKS_CPREKS_MAXITER.brief: Maximum number of rounds of the CP-REKS (Z-vector) solver; exceeding it stops the run with the residual reached.
rules: CP-REKS rounds before an error is raised.
Gap (E_{h}) below which a requested root is computed with a quasi-degeneracy warning.
On a Davidson cassette, also the gap between the last requested and the last computed root below which the computed set grows (§si-solver).
REKS_GRAD_DEGEN_TOL.brief: Gap below which a requested root is flagged as quasi-degenerate.

rules: Largest pair gap (E_{h}) at which the topography table of a NAC pair is printed (§ci-topography).
REKS_CI_TOPOGRAPHY_GAP.brief: Largest gap at which the topography table of a NAC pair is printed.

rules: Moves the listed MOs of the read guess into the active MO columns by column swaps, one token per active orbital, in active-column order; a displaced MO takes the vacated column. Token order sets the pairs (§pairing-scheme, §choose-pairs). The call above is for `reks [4, 4]`.
Tokens: 0-based MO indices or `HOMO`, `LUMO`, `HOMO-k`, `LUMO+k` of the loaded α occupation. The `GUESS READ: active window` line reports the resolved columns and swaps (§diag-wrong-window).
Requires `guess read` (a REKS run stops with a `ValidationError` otherwise); a non-REKS reference ignores the option. C1 only.
If projection onto the current basis drops a read MO as linearly dependent, `REKS READ: WARNING` names it; the later columns shift, and the window may no longer match.
GUESS_ACTIVE_WINDOW.brief: MOs of the read guess placed in the active columns, one token per active orbital: 0-based index, `HOMO-k` or `LUMO+k`.

rules: Parameter δ ≥ 0 of the factor f(x), x = n_{p} n_{q}, that multiplies the coupling Δ of each geminal in the energy (§coupling).
REKS_FON_INTERP_DELTA.brief: Parameter δ of the factor f(n_p n_q) that multiplies the coupling term of each geminal in the REKS energy.

REKS_N_FON.title: REKS_<L>_FON
rules: One option per FON generation (§fon-sets). A non-negative value ℓ is the lower end of the box of the free FON n_{p} of every geminal of that generation (§fons): n_{p} stays variable in [ℓ, 2 − m], m = `REKS_FON_MICRO_BOUND_MARGIN`.

The call above restricts n_{p} of every generation-1 geminal to [1, 2 − m]: it excludes n_{p} < n_{q}, and n_{p} may still reach the closed-shell limit 2 (§diag-fon-inverted). At `REKS_REPORT_LEVEL` ≥ 4 an active floor prints the first line above.
A value above 2 − m is clamped to 2 − m and the FON is frozen there, with the warning above (`REKS_M_FON` 2.5). Negative (the default) disables the bound; the lower end is then m.
REKS_N_FON.brief: Lower bound on the free FON n_p of every geminal of one FON generation (`reks_n_fon`, `reks_m_fon`, …); negative disables it.

REKS_FON_MICRO_NR_MAXITER.brief: Newton iteration cap per geminal block per SCF iteration.

REKS_FON_MICRO_LS_MAXITER.brief: Armijo backtracking (step halving) cap inside one Newton step.

REKS_FON_MICRO_MIN_EIGENVALUE.brief: Floor on the absolute eigenvalues of the reduced Hessian; negative curvature is flipped.

REKS_FON_MICRO_BOUND_MARGIN.brief: Margin m of the SCF FON box [ℓ, 2 − m] kept by the FON micro-solver and the TRAH step, in (0, 1); SI box: `SI_REKS_FON_BOUND_MARGIN`.

SI_REKS_FON_BOUND_MARGIN.brief: Margin m of the box [m, 2 − m] of the SI-only FONs (§si-only-fons) and of their CP-REKS at-bound test, in [0, 1).

REKS_FON_MICRO_BOUNDARY_SKIN.brief: A generation-0 multi-start seed landing within this distance of 0 or 2 counts as boundary-trapped and loses to an interior minimum.

formulas: p_A(i) = \sum_{\mu \in A} \tilde C_{\mu i}^{\,2}, \qquad t_A(a,b) = \sum_{\mu \in A} \tilde C_{\mu a} \tilde C_{\mu b}, \qquad \tilde{\mathbf C} = \mathbf S^{1/2}\mathbf C
rules: After the SCF converges, every orbital pair (a, b) of every generation-0 geminal is tested: IPR_{ab}, the Löwdin inverse participation ratio of the pair, runs over [IPR_{ab}(0) + α − r, IPR_{ab}(0) + α + r] under the rotation θ, and x is the position of the current orbitals in that range (0 = minimum, 1 = maximum). A pair with x > 1/2 is rotated by θ^{*} to the minimum; a pair with r ≤ 64 ε IPR_{ab}(0) (ε the machine epsilon) is left alone. Sweeps over all pairs repeat until one rotates nothing; the FONs are not changed.

First block: the rotated pairs (geminal, 1-based MO numbers, x, θ^{*} in degrees); the SCF then converges again from the rotated orbitals. Without a pair at x > 1/2 the block reads `No geminal orbital pair with x > 1/2.` and no further SCF runs.

Second block: the rotated solution is kept when its SCF converges with E_{SA}(after) < E_{SA}(before) − `E_CONVERGENCE`; otherwise the SCF converges once more from the orbitals before the rotation. The SI step, properties and gradients follow the final solution.

C_{2}H_{4} at 90°, BH&HLYP/6-31G, SSR(2,2) with the all-α determinant, from a localized seed (the active pair of the delocalized solution rotated by 45°, n = 2): without the option the SCF stays there, E_{SA} = −78.351265591745 E_{h}, n_{a} = 2; with it x = 1, θ^{*} = −45°, and the SCF reaches E_{SA} = −78.362111811377 E_{h}, n_{a} = 1, the solution of the 0° → 90° restart chain (first two blocks above).

HF/6-31G(d), seed built the same way from the HF delocalized solution, `REKS_USE_TRAH` with `REKS_GVB_DIIS` false: the localized solution, E_{SA} = −77.884884825216 E_{h}, lies below the delocalized one, −77.879948708032 E_{h}; the SCF from the rotated orbitals (θ^{*} = 45°) returns to the localized solution, and the rotation is rejected (third block).
REKS_GEMINAL_DELOC.brief: After the SCF, rotates generation-0 geminal pairs to their IPR minimum and reconverges; kept if it converges to a lower E_SA.

rules: Selects which REKS blocks appear: the numbers of the run are printed at level 2; levels 3–5 add counters, solver traces and intermediate matrices.
REKS_REPORT_LEVEL.brief: Verbosity of the REKS output, 1–5: from the SCF trace and energetics up to per-iteration solver traces and intermediate matrices.

rules: Trust-region Newton solver (trace tag `TRAH/SHIFT`) for the stationary point of the SA energy in the active–active orbital rotations and the FONs: a box-constrained damped Newton step from the eigendecomposition of the analytic active–active Hessian, a bisection on the damping until the step norm matches the trust radius, and eigenvector following along the inter-pair modes (§nocedal2006-numerical-optimization, Ch. 4 and 11; §baker1986-eigenvector-following; §cerjan1981-transition-states; §helmich-paris2021-trah-scf).

The intra-geminal rotations and the FONs are minimized; their Hessian block enters the step with |λ| of its eigenvalues. When that block has a negative eigenvalue λ (eigenvector v) and ½ |λ| Δ^{2} > `E_CONVERGENCE` (Δ the trust radius), the step s is extended along v to the trust radius, s → s + σ τ v with τ = (Δ^{2} − ‖s‖^{2})^{½} cut back to the variable bounds and σ = −sign(g · v); such a point is left, not reported as converged. After this step the trust radius follows the energy ratio ρ = ΔE / ΔE_{model}.
TRAH steps move the FONs without reordering the orbitals of a geminal (§fons).
Warm-up or whole SCF: §engines.
REKS_USE_TRAH.brief: Trust-region Newton (TRAH) step on the active–active rotations and FONs: warm-up before GVB-DIIS, or the whole SCF without it.

rules: The GVB-DIIS accelerator, the default engine; its formulation is `REKS_DIIS_FORMULATION`.
REKS_GVB_DIIS.brief: GVB-DIIS accelerator of the orbital optimization, in the formulation set by `reks_diis_formulation`.

rules: `ORBITAL` (default; trace tag `ORB-GVB-DIIS`) extrapolates skew-symmetric rotation generators κ directly in the MO basis and bypasses Fock diagonalization each step (§ionova1995-orbital-diis; the r-GDIIS variant of §sethio2024-r-gdiis).

`CFM` (trace tag `CFM-GVB-DIIS/SHIFT`) extrapolates the composite multishell Fock matrix, the multishell-Fock DIIS of §muller1994-gvb-diis, where every active orbital is its own shell (core = 1 shell, virtual = 1 shell).
REKS_DIIS_FORMULATION.brief: GVB-DIIS formulation: extrapolation of the orbital-rotation generators κ, or of the composite multishell Fock matrix (`CFM`).

rules: SCF iteration at which GVB-DIIS takes over from the burn-in or from TRAH (§engines).
REKS_GVB_DIIS_START.brief: First SCF iteration of GVB-DIIS; earlier iterations run the level-shifted burn-in or TRAH.

REKS_GVB_LEVEL_SHIFT.brief: Shell gap of the multishell Fock matrix in the `CFM` formulation of GVB-DIIS.
rules: Artificial shell gap of the CFM multishell Fock matrix, separate from `LEVEL_SHIFT`; unused with `REKS_DIIS_FORMULATION` `ORBITAL` (the default).

True: the base shift equals `LEVEL_SHIFT` through iteration 3; afterwards it decays (factor 0.5–0.95) when the previous iteration had no orbital swaps and maximal active mixing below 0.15, and grows by a factor 1.5 when the previous iteration had swaps or mixing above 0.30; it stays within [0.01, `LEVEL_SHIFT`].
False holds the base shift at `LEVEL_SHIFT` for every iteration.
LEVEL_SHIFT_ADAPT.brief: Adaptive base of the staircase level shift: decays while the orbitals are stable, grows back up to `level_shift` on swaps or strong mixing.

REKS_DIIS_ACTIVATION.brief: Criterion for `ORBITAL` GVB-DIIS to take over from the TRAH warm-up: the iteration count alone, or also the orbital gradient.
rules: When `ORBITAL` GVB-DIIS takes over from the TRAH warm-up: `ITERATION` at iteration `REKS_GVB_DIIS_START`; `GRADIENT` from that iteration on, once ‖g_{orb}‖_{F} < `REKS_DIIS_CFM_ACTIVATION_GORB`. Inert without `REKS_USE_TRAH` and with `CFM`, which always waits for the gradient.

REKS_DIIS_CFM_ACTIVATION_GORB.brief: Orbital-gradient norm ‖g_orb‖_F below which GVB-DIIS takes over from the TRAH warm-up.
rules: Threshold on ‖g_{orb}‖_{F} for GVB-DIIS to take over from the TRAH warm-up once `REKS_GVB_DIIS_START` is reached: always with `CFM`, with `ORBITAL` only under `REKS_DIIS_ACTIVATION` `GRADIENT`. Inert without `REKS_USE_TRAH`.

REKS_GVB_ROBUST_VERDICT.brief: Enables the post-hoc verdict that rewinds extrapolated GVB-DIIS steps whose orbital gradient grows.
rules: Post-hoc acceptance verdict on extrapolated GVB-DIIS steps; its trip ratio is `REKS_DIIS_MON_VERDICT_RHO` (§option-table).

REKS_DIIS_COND_ANGLE_FILTER.brief: Enables the angle filter with stale-drop that prunes near-dependent and stale GVB-DIIS error vectors.

REKS_DIIS_COND_ANGLE_CUTOFF.brief: Angle-filter cutoff c_s: smallest sine of the angle to the kept differences for a GVB-DIIS error vector to stay.

REKS_DIIS_COND_STALE_DELTA.brief: Stale-drop threshold δ: GVB-DIIS error vectors with norm above the newest norm / √δ are dropped; 0 switches it off.

REKS_DIIS_COND_KAPPA_BYPASS.brief: Condition number of the GVB-DIIS error matrix above which the SVD-conditioned solve replaces the plain bordered solve.

REKS_DIIS_COND_SVD_RCOND.brief: Relative singular-value cutoff of the SVD-conditioned GVB-DIIS solve.

REKS_DIIS_COND_COEFF_NORM_MAX.brief: Bound c_max on the GVB-DIIS coefficient norm |c|², also used by the angle filter to drop near-duplicate error vectors.

REKS_DIIS_COND_TIKHONOV.brief: Enables the Tikhonov ridge on the SVD-conditioned GVB-DIIS solve.

REKS_DIIS_COND_TIKHONOV_SCALE.brief: Ridge magnitude of the Tikhonov-regularized GVB-DIIS SVD solve; 0 applies no ridge.

REKS_DIIS_MON_VERDICT_RHO.brief: Verdict trip ratio: a GVB-DIIS step is rewound when ‖g_orb‖ exceeds this multiple of its maximum over the recent iterates.

REKS_DIIS_MON_VERDICT_STREAK.brief: Consecutive verdict rewinds without a new best iterate before GVB-DIIS restarts from the best iterate.

REKS_DIIS_MON_SUPPRESS_WINDOW.brief: Iterations after a GVB-DIIS rewind, restart or switch during which the verdict is suspended.

REKS_DIIS_MON_NONMONOTONE_M.brief: Depth M of the nonmonotone references of the GVB-DIIS monitors: max ‖g_orb‖ and min E_SA over the last M iterates.

REKS_GVB_GATE_STREAK.brief: Consecutive iterations meeting the energy and gradient thresholds before GVB-DIIS reports convergence.

REKS_DIIS_GUARD_LATCH_GRACE.brief: Consecutive iterations without the basin signal after which the GVB-DIIS outcome guard clears its basin latch.

REKS_DIIS_GUARD_LANDING_TOLERANCE.brief: Relative tolerance at which a GVB-DIIS rewind landing counts as a repeat (best E_SA and best ‖g_orb‖ reproduced).

REKS_DIIS_MON_PROGRESS_EPS.brief: Sufficient-decrease fraction ε: a GVB-DIIS iterate counts as progress only if ‖g_orb‖ ≤ (1 − ε) × best ‖g_orb‖.

REKS_DIIS_FON_BRANCH_CUTOFF.brief: FON displacement from the best iterate at or above which the GVB-DIIS guard reads an energy drop as a basin transition.

REKS_DIIS_RESTART_BUDGET.brief: GVB-DIIS monitor restarts without sufficient improvement allowed before the monitors stop and rewind once to the best iterate.

REKS_DIIS_MON_CYCLE.brief: Enables the GVB-DIIS no-progress / step-cap monitor, which restarts from the best iterate.

REKS_DIIS_MON_CYCLE_WINDOW.brief: Iterations without a new best ‖g_orb‖ before the GVB-DIIS cycle monitor restarts from the best iterate.

REKS_DIIS_MON_CYCLE_CAP_STREAK.brief: Consecutive `ORBITAL` step-cap hits before the GVB-DIIS cycle monitor restarts.

REKS_DIIS_ORB_BASE_MAP_DAMP.brief: Damping α of the `ORBITAL` GVB-DIIS Newton step from the re-anchored frame after a restart.
